title: BlueBanyan Labs — on‑prem scaling & Terraform appendix (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is an internal draft for BlueBanyan Labs (R&D cluster) — candidate private deployment for Q2 2025. Focus: practical on‑prem sizing guidance, Terraform module refactor notes, upgrade/cutover plan, and a short architecture Q&A for BlueBanyan engineering leads.

High level goals / SLOs (customer requirements summarized)
- 95th percentile token latencies: <75ms for short chat flows (<=256 tokens), target burst latencies <150ms for 1024 tokens.
- Baseline throughput: 80 sequences/sec sustained (1000 token avg) for peak experiments.
- Availability: 99.5% monthly for inference plane.
- Data isolation: all inference traffic inside BlueBanyan network, CMK for model keys.
- Minimum on‑prem retention of logs/metrics 90 days.

Assumptions used for sizing (callouts)
- Typical request: 2.5k tokens/session (because research jobs often do long injections), but majority of interactive traffic is 128–512 tokens. We weight capacity for a 70/30 split short/long.
- Model: they requested variant of Llama‑derived 70B dense model; we expect to serve quantized 8-bit and 4-bit variants depending on test stage.
- KV cache: heavy reuse expected from repeated prompt prefixes. Cache hit target ~40% for early runs.
- Deployment hardware is per‑rack: 8x H100 (80GB) or 16x A100 (80GB) depending on procurement window. Networking: 100GbE spine with 25/50GbE leaf.

Recommended baseline cluster layout (initial phase)
- Option A (preferred for perf): 2 racks, each with 8x H100 (total 16 H100). Use 2 inference pools: "high‑mem‑low‑latency" and "dense‑batching".
  - High‑mem‑low‑latency: 6 GPUs/rack (12 total) pinned to low‑latency policy for interactive chat.
  - Dense‑batching: remaining GPUs serve batch workloads/experiments with larger max seq lengths.
- Option B (capital constrained): 2 racks, 16x A100 (80GB) with same pool split; expect ~1.1–1.3x latency increase for some models.

Storage & network sizing
- Local NVMe per node: 4TB for model staging and checkpoint transient caches.
- Shared object store: S3-compatible (minio) with 300TB initial capacity, lifecycle to archive after 90 days.
- Networking: 100GbE between racks; 25GbE to edge load balancers. Plan for 20Gbps sustained egress headroom from each rack during peak.

Token throughput math (back of envelope)
- Target sustained tokens/sec = 80 sequences/sec * 1000 tokens = 80k tokens/sec.
- With 16 H100 and dynamic batching + KV caching we estimate ~5k tokens/sec per GPU for this model in 8-bit quant mode => 16 * 5k = 80k. Margin: +15% for headroom -> target 18 GPUs.
- If using A100 in place of H100, per‑GPU tokens/sec drops ~20% -> need additional GPUs or accept higher latency.

Terraform module notes (refactor suggestions & constraints)
- Current modules: rw_infra_onprem_v1 (monolith) — brittle for per‑customer overrides.
- Proposal: split into 3 composable modules: network (vpc, routing, firewall), compute (gpu pools, node config, driver), and platform (model-storage, kms, metrics forwarding). Keep state per‑customer in separate backend (s3/minio + locking via consul).
- Inputs to expose: gpu_type, pool_sizes(list), model_mount_path, kms_key_arn, external_lb_ip, telemetry_endpoint.
- Outputs: api_gateway_ip, lb_dns, kms_key_id, model_registry_bucket.
- Versioning: tag modules with semver and require explicit module version in customer's root. Avoid using local module paths in customer deliverables.
- Security: require ephemeral credentials for Terraform runs via OIDC to reduce long‑lived tokens. Document a step to rotate service account keys post initial apply.
- Upgrade strategy in TF: encourage use of blue/green by deploying a new compute pool, draining traffic, and switching DNS/LB targets; avoid in‑place GPU driver upgrades during business hours.

Edge cases / gotchas observed on previous customers
- NVMe firmware upgrades can require node reboot; schedule outside experiments.
- MinIO/Gateway metadata locks can choke model staging if manifest writes are concurrent — include a retry/backoff and idempotency in staging script.
- Quantized models may need specific CUDA/cuFFT versions — tie module parameter gpu_driver_version to validated matrix.

Rollout and upgrade plan (cutover)
1) Preflight (2–3 weeks)
   - Confirm rack power & PDU capacity (SLA with procurement).
   - Run Terraform dry‑runs with simulated module inputs in staging account.
   - Validate model artifacts (shrinkwrap) and quantization artifacts uploaded to customer S3.
   - Security review: CMK provisioning & access policy review by BlueBanyan sec team (ticket INFRA-4321).

2) Initial deploy (Week 0)
   - Apply network + platform modules (minio, kms, dns).
   - Deploy compute pools with label "canary" (2 GPUs per rack) and run smoke tests.
   - Gradually scale compute pool to target.

3) Validation (Week 1)
   - Traffic shape tests: synthetic generator to emulate 70/30 short/long split.
   - Perf regressions: run curated prompt set used by Product (see confluence link).
   - Eviction/oom tests: intentionally allocate >100% mem for one worker to ensure graceful restart.

4) Cutover (Week 2)
   - Point LB to new cluster via DNS TTL swap (3–5min TTL).
   - Monitor for 60min, fallback plan: revert DNS to previous LB or scale down new pool.

Rollback plan
- If severe regressions: immediate DNS revert + scale down new pool.
- If model corruption observed: restore model artifacts from previous S3 snapshot (we keep last 3 snapshots).
- Maintain rollback runbook in /runbooks/bluebanyan-rollback.md (SRE to own updates).

Observability & validation metrics
- Must export: per‑model latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec per GPU, KV cache hit ratio, GC pauses, cgroup memory high events.
- Alert thresholds: P95 > 200ms (warn), P95 > 300ms (critical); GPU mem OOM > 0.5% events within 1h critical.
- Synthetic canary set: 25 prompts that exercise few-shot, function calling, long generation — run every 5m, results into canary dashboard.

Q&A (from BlueBanyan engineering)
Q: What happens if they later request servo‑grade H300s?
A: Terraform modules should accept gpu_type and image mapping; drivers/kernel pairing must be validated in a compatibility matrix. H300s likely require different kernel patches; plan a one‑week compatibility window.

Q: How to handle multi‑tenant experiments on shared cluster?
A: Use namespace/cgroup isolation, RBAC for model registry, and optional tenant quotas via the LB layer. Prefer separate pools for noisy tenants.

Outstanding questions / decisions (TO DO)
- Confirm procurement timeline: H100 vs A100 (procurement ticket).
- Decide retention windows for model stage artifacts (90 vs 30 days).
- Finalize CMK ownership model: BlueBanyan‑managed vs Redwood‑managed.
- Agree on Terraform remote state backend (minio vs managed S3).

Next actions (short list)
- [Evan] Draft PR with modular TF changes targeting rw-terraform-modules (see linked PR).
- [Ravi] Kick off power/PDU validation with BlueBanyan Facilities this week.
- [Mariana] Prepare canary prompt set and synthetic generator harness.
- Schedule 1hr prep call with BlueBanyan infra leads (available windows: Tue/Thu next two weeks).

Notes to self / loose brainstorming
- Could expose a "gpu_utilization_slo" variable to auto‑suggest pool sizes in module using simple heuristics.
- Consider an init container that validates quant artifacts at node‑boot to reduce staging surprises.
- Add a small playbook for NVMe health checks (SMART + throughput) into the platform module.

Attachments / references:
- INFRA-4321 (procurement + security review)
- PR #214 in rw-terraform-modules (module split draft)
- Confluence page: private-deploy/bluebanyan-onprem-specs

End of draft — please add comments inline.
